Jonas / Ben — reviewed the redlines and tax cert. Quick legal take and suggested contract language below. This is intended to be implementable without changing the MSA:

1) Invoice recipient appendix (suggested):
"Invoice Recipient(s): Seller shall issue invoices to the invoice recipients listed in Appendix A. Where usage is attributable to an EU-resident entity of Buyer, Seller shall issue such invoice to Buyer EU Entity. Where usage is attributable to Buyer US Entity, Seller shall issue such invoice to Buyer US Entity. Buyer shall provide tax residency certificates on request to support VAT treatment."

2) VAT / reverse charge: We are comfortable relying on Buyer-provided VAT/residency evidence upon request and including an indemnity if evidence is not provided or is later found incorrect. Seller is not able to self-assess EU reverse-charge absent Buyer evidence. Proposed clause:
"VAT Treatment and Evidence: Buyer shall provide valid tax residency certificates upon request. Where Buyer provides such evidence, Seller will not charge VAT and will apply reverse-charge treatment where applicable. Buyer shall indemnify Seller for any VAT, penalties, or interest arising from Buyer’s failure to provide accurate evidence."

3) Net terms: If Acme requires Net 45, Sales should confirm account approval. From a legal standpoint both Net 30 and Net 45 are acceptable; any change affects invoicing cadence and potential collections terms to be reflected in Appendix A.

I can prepare a redline incorporating the above and a two-Order-Form vs single-Order-Form appendix for finance to choose. Ben — flag any operational blockers for two invoice recipients on one contract.

-Kimberly
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference
